3.text: 2. Ureˊtvik (“in the lengthening”). This corresponds to the second month.

11.text: 9. Êh-ɪˊntok (“with the fresh air going out”).
11.resolved: Êh-ɪˊntok: Ê = E + U+0302 circumflex (capital); ɪ = U+026A dotless small-cap, confirmed at 4x against dotted i's in the gloss 'with'/'fresh'; ˊ = U+02CA stress after ɪ

12.resolved: Ñerg̣eˊrɪk: Ñ = N + U+0303 tilde (capital); g̣ = g + U+0323 dot below, confirmed at 4x after the advisory flagged this word as a rare form — the dot was missed on first read; ˊ = U+02CA stress after the second e; ɪ = U+026A dotless small-cap in rɪk

13.resolved: Tur-äᵋleˊtɪk: ä = a + U+0308 diaeresis; ᵋ = U+1D4B laryngeal superscript immediately after ä (raised loop-with-tail shape, matching the corpus's documented 'reads as superscript g at small scale' pattern for this exact mark rather than any catalogued g-sort); ˊ = U+02CA stress after e (culminative, one per word — the ä mark is independent of it); ɪ = U+026A dotless small-cap in tɪk
13.note: The raised mark after ä has no catalogued 'superscript g' codepoint anywhere in the inventory (keying_spec.md §5.9/§2.1); keyed as the laryngeal U+1D4B per the documented ä+laryngeal pattern (cf. spec's own 'äˊᵋq-iˊmɪl' example) rather than left uncatalogued, since a catalogued sort fits both the position (immediately after a vowel) and does not violate the one-stress-per-word rule. Flagging for adjudicator: this identification rests on shape-at-4x and the corpus pattern, not certainty — same mark recurs identically on line 15.

14.resolved: G̣ɪthaˊk: G̣ = G + U+0323 dot below (capital), confirmed at 4x; ɪ = U+026A dotless small-cap; ˊ = U+02CA stress after a

15.resolved: Läᵋleˊñkɪ: ä = a + U+0308; ᵋ = U+1D4B laryngeal after ä, same shape and reasoning as line 13's äᵋ; ˊ = U+02CA stress after e; ñ = n + U+0303; ɪ = U+026A dotless small-cap
15.note: Same open-doubt as line 13's ᵋ reading — flagging both together for the adjudicator; the two occurrences on this page are visually identical, which supports (but does not prove) the same reading for both.
